newsitem.title: FRANCE: French press divided on Euro row.
newsitem.headline: French press divided on Euro row.

text.p: French newspapers reacted on Tuesday according to their political sympathies to France's request to its EU partners for a delay in the stability pact intended to underpin European monetary union.
The conservative Le Figaro, generally hostile to France's new left-wing cabinet, wrote: "There will be no state of grace for (Socialist Prime Minister) Lionel Jospin."

The new French government threw the debate over economic and monetary union (EMU) into confusion on Monday when it said it needed time to study the stability pact, designed to keep budget defifits under control after the launch of the single currency.

"Europe has given itself rules which ban laxism or lack of seriousness in the administration of public affairs. Lionel Jospin would have been well advised to take this into consideration during his election campaign," Le Figaro wrote.
"This would have allowed him to avoid making all sorts of outlandish promises which will only serve as ingredients to create the social timebombs of tomorrow."

The newspaper warned in a front-page editorial: "The noose now tightening around the new cabinet's neck is that it must either honour its election promises and open a crisis with Europe or apply Europe's rules in France and provoke a rise in the country of disappointments whose consequences are impossible to predict,"
The left-of-centre Liberation, which strongly supports Jospin, said: "It's not yet a crisis (with Europe) but it could be."
However, the newspaper said Economy Minister Dominique Strauss-Kahn's demands were not extravagant.
"Yes, France has asked for a delay to think. But it has accepted the main point so it's not exactly what one would call a break-up," Liberation wrote.

"After such a clear vote in France and with Europe dominated by social democrats, the narrow free-market spirit which presided over the conclusion of the Maastricht Treaty must necessarily give in a bit."
